title_en: Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Promoting the Reform of the Diversion of Complex and Simple Cases in Administrative Litigation Procedures
keywords_en: administrative litigation; application for retrial; jurisdiction
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Opinions on Promoting the Reform of Streamlining Administrative Litigation Procedures

Fa Fa [2021] No. 17

To deepen the reform of the administrative litigation system, promote the streamlining of administrative cases by separating complex from simple, prioritizing cases by gravity, and allocating cases to fast or slow tracks, optimize the allocation of administrative adjudication resources, promote the substantive resolution of administrative disputes, lawfully protect the lawful rights and interests of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations, and support and supervise administrative organs in law-based administration, these Opinions are formulated in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Administrative Procedure Law) and the provisions of judicial interpretations, and in light of the actual work of adjudication.

I. General Provisions

Article 1. People's courts shall strictly regulate the adjudication of complex administrative cases, lawfully and quickly adjudicate simple administrative cases, improve the rules for the application of summary procedures in administrative litigation, promote the application of electronic litigation, guide parties to correctly exercise their litigation rights and lawfully fulfill their litigation obligations, and comprehensively improve the quality, efficiency, and credibility of administrative adjudication.

Article 2. When a people's court of first instance adjudicates the following administrative cases, it may adjudicate them as simple cases:

(1) Cases falling under the circumstances provided for in Article 82, paragraphs 1 and 2, of the Administrative Procedure Law;
(2) Cases that do not meet the statutory conditions for filing a lawsuit;
(3) Cases involving不服 (dissatisfaction with) a decision of an administrative reconsideration organ to reject a reconsideration application or to dismiss a reconsideration petition;
(4) Cases concerning government information disclosure, performance of statutory duties, and trademark authorization and confirmation that involve clear facts, clear rights and obligations, and no major dispute.

When a people's court of second instance adjudicates appeals against judgments of the first instance that were handled as simple cases under the fast-track procedure, cases where the party withdraws the appeal, withdraws the lawsuit, or the case is treated as a withdrawal of appeal by default, and appeals against rulings on non-acceptance of a case, dismissal of a lawsuit, or jurisdictional objections, it may adjudicate them as simple cases.

Higher people's courts may explore conducting the work of streamlining administrative retrial applications into complex and simple categories.

Article 3. People's courts may establish fast-track adjudication teams for administrative cases, or specialized or categorized adjudication teams, or may appoint case streamliners responsible for the diversion of complex and simple administrative cases, to achieve fast adjudication of simple cases, specialized adjudication of categorized cases, and refined adjudication of complex cases.

II. Promoting Pre-litigation Diversion of Administrative Disputes

Article 4. People's courts shall strengthen the governance of the sources of administrative disputes, improve the mechanisms for the diversion and connection between administrative litigation and non-litigation dispute resolution methods such as administrative reconsideration and administrative adjudication, explore the establishment of pre-litigation reconciliation mechanisms, rely on the benign interaction between the judiciary and the administration, and strengthen the diversified resolution of administrative disputes and the construction of related platforms.

Article 5. For cases that may be mediated as provided for in the Administrative Procedure Law, cases where the administrative counterpart seeks reconciliation, or cases where handling through reconciliation is more conducive to the substantive resolution of administrative disputes, the people's court may, before filing the case, guide the parties to settle the matter voluntarily or through mediation by a third party. Pre-litigation mediation shall be conducted on a mediation platform and shall be assigned a corresponding case number.

A positive incentive mechanism for the voluntary performance of non-litigation mediation shall be established. By incorporating voluntary performance into the credit evaluation system and other means, the parties shall be guided to perform the mediation agreement voluntarily and promptly, thereby timely resolving administrative disputes.

Article 6. Where a settlement agreement is reached through pre-litigation mediation and the parties jointly apply for judicial confirmation, the people's court may, in accordance with the law, confirm the validity of the settlement agreement and issue a pre-litigation mediation document for administrative cases.

If a party refuses mediation or fails to reach a settlement agreement, and the statutory conditions for filing a lawsuit are met, the people's court shall, in accordance with the law, promptly register the case.

After the case is filed, if a party applies for withdrawal of the lawsuit through mediation, and the people's court, upon review, finds that it complies with the law, it shall render a ruling granting the withdrawal of the lawsuit.

Article 7. During pre-litigation mediation, facts that are undisputed by the parties shall be recorded in the mediation records and confirmed by the signatures of the parties.

During the trial process, with the consent of the parties, the undisputed facts confirmed during the mediation process shall no longer be subject to evidence presentation and cross-examination, except for facts admitted by a party as a compromise to reach a settlement agreement, or where there is sufficient evidence to the contrary to overturn the fact.

III. Improving Application Rules for Summary Procedures

Article 8. Where a people's court applies summary procedures in accordance with Article 82, paragraph 1, of the Administrative Procedure Law to adjudicate an administrative case, it may send a notice of adjudication under summary procedures to the parties, informing them of the method of adjudication, the time limit for adjudication, and other matters.

Where a people's court, in accordance with Article 82, paragraph 2, of the Administrative Procedure Law, adjudicates other first-instance administrative cases, it shall seek the opinions of the parties. The solicitation of opinions may be conducted through simple methods such as the litigation platform, telephone, text message, instant messaging account, etc. Where a party does not agree to the application of summary procedures, it shall submit a statement to the people's court within five days from the date of receipt of the notice. If no objection is raised within the time limit, the people's court may proceed with adjudication under summary procedures.

Article 9. When a people's court applies summary procedures to adjudicate an administrative case, it may, depending on the circumstances of the case, adopt the following methods to simplify the court trial procedure, but shall protect the parties' litigation rights such as the right to defend, present evidence, cross-examine, state, and debate:

(1) If the verification of the parties' identities, notification of rights and obligations, and announcement of court trial discipline have already been completed during the pre-trial preparation stage or by other means, there is no need to repeat them at the opening of the trial;
(2) The court trial shall directly focus on the disputed issues related to the legality of the challenged administrative act, and the court investigation and court debate may be conducted together.

If both parties indicate that they do not need a period for defense or a period for providing evidence, the people's court may directly proceed with the trial, and the trial time shall not be limited by the defense period or the evidence provision period.

For cases adjudicated under summary procedures, the trial shall be concluded in one session, unless the people's court deems it necessary to hold another session.

Article 10. The audio and video recordings of the trial of an administrative case adjudicated under summary procedures may, with the consent of the parties, replace the court trial record.

Article 11. When a people's court applies summary procedures to adjudicate an administrative case, it may simplify the judgment document, but it shall include the basic information of the parties, the litigation claims, the defense opinions, the main facts, a brief reasoning, the legal basis and the operative part of the judgment, as well as the allocation of litigation costs and the necessary content such as informing the parties of their right to appeal.

Article 12. For a case converted from summary procedures to ordinary procedures, the litigation acts carried out before the conversion are effective. Facts undisputed and confirmed by both parties may no longer be subject to evidence presentation and cross-examination.

A case converted from summary procedures to ordinary procedures shall not be converted back to summary procedures.

IV. Fast-track Trial of Simple Cases in Accordance with Law

Article 13. After reviewing the case files, conducting investigations, or questioning the parties, if the people's court finds that the plaintiff's lawsuit does not meet the statutory conditions for filing, it may directly issue a ruling to dismiss the lawsuit, except where the relevant facts need to be ascertained through a court trial.

Article 14. If the verification of the parties' identities, notification of rights and obligations, and exchange of evidence have already been completed during the pre-trial preparation stage, they shall not be repeated at the opening of the trial.

Evidence that has been confirmed as undisputed and recorded in the files during the pre-trial preparation stage may be used as the basis for determining case facts if the court explains it during the court investigation and the parties confirm it.

Article 15. For cases where the reconsideration organ is a co-defendant, if the facts confirmed by the reconsideration decision are consistent with those found by the original administrative act, and the opposing party expressly acknowledges them during the trial, the people's court may simplify the presentation and cross-examination of evidence in court, except where there is sufficient evidence to the contrary to overturn the facts.

Article 16. For appeal cases that meet any of the following circumstances, after reviewing the case files, conducting investigations, or questioning the parties, if no new facts, evidence, or reasons are presented, the people's court may adjudicate without holding a trial:

(1) The appeal is against a first-instance administrative ruling;
(2) The party contends that the first-instance judgment or ruling incorrectly applied laws or regulations.

While ensuring the parties' litigation rights, the people's court of second instance may question the parties through simple methods such as the litigation platform, telephone, text message, or instant messaging account, and record it in the file, except where new facts or new evidence are involved.

Article 17. When a people's court reviews an application for retrial, it shall conduct the review in accordance with Article 91 of the Administrative Procedure Law, considering the applicant's retrial request and reasons. If it is necessary to question the parties, this may be done through simple methods such as the litigation platform, telephone, text message, or instant messaging account.

If the grounds for retrial asserted by the party are clearly untenable, or do not meet the conditions for applying for retrial, the ruling dismissing the retrial application may be appropriately simplified, but shall include the basic information of the parties, the source of the case, the applicant's request and reasons for the retrial, a brief reasoning, the legal basis, and the operative part of the ruling, among other necessary content.

Article 18. For simple administrative cases adjudicated under the fast-track procedure, the court trial record may be appropriately simplified. The relevant audio and video recordings of the trial shall be made into storage media such as CDs and filed together with the case file.

Article 19. For administrative cases concerning government information disclosure, failure to perform statutory duties, non-acceptance or procedural dismissal of reconsideration applications, and trademark authorization and confirmation, where the facts are clear, rights and obligations are clear, and there is no major dispute, the people's court may conduct the trial by referring to the elements of legality review of the challenged administrative act and the disputed focus of the parties, and may produce element-based administrative judgment documents.

Element-based administrative judgment documents may adopt a simplified format, to be filled in according to the basic elements of administrative judgment documents such as the status of the parties, litigation claims, basic facts, reasoning, and judgment results.

Article 20. If different parties file separate lawsuits against the same administrative act or the same category of administrative acts, they may be docketed together, and the same adjudication team may conduct centralized scheduling, trial, adjudication, and pronouncement of judgment.

Article 21. During the process of adjudicating a simple administrative case, if the people's court discovers that the case is complex or difficult, it shall promptly convert it into a complex case for adjudication. If it is necessary to change the collegial panel or the judge, the parties shall be informed.

Article 22. When the people's court, the parties, and other litigation participants conduct administrative litigation activities online through an information-based litigation platform, matters not provided for in the Administrative Procedure Law may be handled by reference to the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law and the streamlining of civil litigation procedures.

V. Supplementary Provisions

Article 23. These Opinions shall take effect on June 1, 2021.

May 14, 2021
